text:
marta: quick sync — we need to lock the next 2-week post-deploy iteration. two competing asks: focus the first sprint on high-sev bug backlog (customer-facing regressions) OR push customer-requested enhancements + a small tech-debt slice. thoughts?

sanjay: i'd favor bug-first for 1 week then pivot to enhancements. reduces risk and reduces interrupt for infra.

carol: support data — 6 customers opened severity-2 issues since launch, 2 are repeat regressions. if we keep waiting we get more churn.

lucas: quick numbers: blocking bugs = ~18 dev-hours to fully remediate (estimated), enhancements = ~60 dev-hours but higher NPS impact for 3 paying accounts.

ana: UX perspective — enhancements are mostly polish for paid flows; shipping them increases conversion in short term but not urgent.

marta: proposal: adopt a split plan, not all-or-nothing. concrete: reserve 30% of capacity for immediate P1/P2 bug queue and prioritize top-3 customer fixes. remaining 70% goes to a focused enhancements slice (2 features) + 1 tech-debt task. agree?

sanjay: +1 to a hard reserve. request: make the reserve interrupt-light — only on-calls can pull P1s into enhancements work.

carol: please tie fixes to customer communications. i'll own the follow-ups if we commit to timelines.

marta: here's an extremely small rubric to make decisions during the sprint:
```
Priority decision rubric (short):
1) Severity (P1/P2) for live customers -> immediate reserve
2) Revenue signal (existing paying customer impact) -> next
3) Effort/ROI (low-effort high-ROI wins) -> schedule into enhancement bucket
4) Regressions that increase error rate >5% -> auto-promote
```

lucas: can we surface a dashboard widget for this? a single table showing open P1s + impacted customers + est dev hours. should be trivial.

marta: yes — if lucas can mock the widget by EOD we can use it for daily standups. assign owner: lucas for dashboard, sanjay for on-call pull policy, carol for comms.

ana: design note — for the two enhancement slices: 1) faster checkout CTA, 2) improved error messaging. both low-design risk.

product-bot: deploy: canary rollout v1.2.3 completed to 10% prod at 2024-06-12T14:03:21Z :white_check_mark:

marta: final ask: if we see >3 P1s in first 72h, we flip to a full bug-sprint for the remainder. otherwise proceed with split plan. everyone good?

sanjay: good by me.

carol: good. i'll prep a customer note template.

lucas: i'll have the dashboard stub by EOD and add an alert for P1 count.

ana: ok from design.

marta: thanks — i'll post the sprint brief and update the board (kanban) after standup. :thumbsup:
